statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup. Let e be the number of minimal generators of S, let c be the smallest integer such that every integer greater than or equal to c belongs to S, and let L be the set of elements of S that are strictly less than c. Then e multiplied by the number of elements of L is at least c.

domain_restrictions: S must be a numerical semigroup: subset of nonnegative integers, contains 0, closed under addition, with finite complement in Z_{>=0}
minimal generating set of S is finite and its cardinality is e (so e ∈ Z_{>=1})
c is the conductor (smallest integer with all larger integers in S) and exists because Z_{>=0}\S is finite
L is finite: L = S ∩ [0, c-1]
cardinality |L| denotes the number of elements of L (a nonnegative integer)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all S ⊆ Z_{>=0} with 0 ∈ S, closed under addition, and Z_{>=0}\S finite, let e = |MinGen(S)|, let c = min{ n ∈ Z : ∀ m ≥ n, m ∈ S }, and let L = S ∩ [0,c-1]. Then e * |L| ≥ c.
quantifier_order: forall S (S is a numerical semigroup, i.e. S ⊆ Z_{>=0}, 0 ∈ S, closed under addition, Z_{>=0} \ S finite)
define c := min{ n ∈ Z : ∀ m ≥ n, m ∈ S } (exists because Z_{>=0}\S finite)
